_comment: Sample 90-day sales for the live parts list. Invented figures, real
SKUs. Weekly velocity is units_sold x 7 / 90, kept exact.
Amazon rows are keyed by Amazon's own channel SKU, which is what
Veeqo reports and what listings.yaml maps; the internal SKU is used
only where Amazon holds no listing (Shopify and direct).

rows._comment: Components sold on their own, not inside a kit.

_comment: DECOYS. Rows keyed on Zach's OWN part number for the three C-A-T
colourways, which Amazon does not use and Shannon must never read.
Every figure here is deliberately WRONG and deliberately unequal to
the sum of that colourway's channel SKUs below, so a report that
reads one of these rows is a report with a visibly different number
in it. Delete these rows and nothing may change; that is the test.
NAR owns the C-A-T listings, three colourways share ASINs and no
title states a colour, so these SKUs are the ONLY thing keeping
black, orange and blue apart. Black 138+47=185, orange 53+29+11=93,
blue 61+24=85: three sums, all different from each other and from
every decoy above, so no wrong join can produce a right answer.
